claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has excellent mechanical properties at room temperature and approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is complete substitution of Ta by Nb while retaining equiatomic Hf, Mo, Ti, and Zr, producing HfMoNbTiZr.
Ta-to-Nb substitution will reduce alloy density by approximately 5–10%.
HfMoNbTiZr will retain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Nb substitution will preserve dislocation–solute interactions.
Nb substitution will preserve high-temperature phase stability up to approximately 1000 °C.
Nb has a density of approximately 8.57 g/cm³, whereas Ta has a density of approximately 16.65 g/cm³.
Nb has an atomic radius similar to that of Ta.
The similar atomic radii of Nb and Ta allow Nb to enter the lattice without disrupting its BCC structure.
Replacing Ta with lower-density Nb reduces the heavy-element mass contribution to the alloy.
Preservation of the BCC structure and dislocation–solute interactions will maintain the strengthening mechanisms responsible for yield strength and ductility at elevated temperature.
HfMoNbTiZr will have yield strength comparable to or slightly greater than that of HfMoTaTiZr from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
HfMoNbTiZr will have ductility comparable to or slightly greater than that of HfMoTaTiZr from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain creep resistance comparable to or slightly better than that of HfMoTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is restricted to conventional as-cast material tested under standard quasi-static or creep loading from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C.

A density reduction below approximately 3%, a decrease greater than 10% in yield strength or ductility, or phase instability relative to HfMoTaTiZr under the specified conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
